knowledge_point.title: Solving Exponential Equations Containing Different Bases by Rewriting One Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
To solve this equation, we need both exponential terms to have a common base.

To do this, we write $81$ as ${3}^{4},$ and then we rewrite the right-hand side using the power rule of exponents:

$$
\begin{aligned}{81}^{2a} & =\frac{1}{{3}^{a-1}} \\ {({3}^{4})}^{2a} & =\frac{1}{{3}^{a-1}} \\ {3}^{8a} & =\frac{1}{{3}^{a-1}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we rewrite the right-hand side using a negative exponent: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{8a} & ={3}^{-(a-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(3),$ we equate the exponents and solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}8a & =-(a-1) \\ 8a & =-a+1 \\ 9a & =1 \\ a & =\frac{1}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: positive integer base > 1; exactly one base is rewritten; nonzero unique rational root
